break.interpretation: Ablating the original components leaves the target logit almost unchanged under this phrasing, so the original path has lost its measured causal effect.

layerShiftRescue.interpretation: Shifting the same components across neighbouring layers recovers the effect, so the break is a layer misplacement.

pathChange.interpretation: The replacement path uses components that do not overlap the source circuit.

items.whyStatement: Under the embedded-question phrasing of the Germany prompt the original path (MLP L31 n9943 + attention L20 h24) broke as a magnitude-collapse: the remapped replay drop was 0.0000 against 0.4375 on the source prompt. A layer shift of -1 alone recovered the effect. The replacement search found a path (MLP L31 n8967 + attention L31 h22) with target-logit drop 0.3125; relative to the source circuit this is a component-rebinding: layers [20, 31] -> [31] (later), 0/2 components retained, ablate positions [5] -> [19]. On held-out families the replacement path passed 4/5; failing families: sentence-completion.
items.claimBoundary: This entry explains where the measured target-logit causal effect moved between two recorded prompts of one subject. It is not semantic proof of what the components compute, not proof of a unique circuit, and not evidence about families, subjects, or models beyond those measured here.
